# Preparing for demographic history analysis
I'm gonna use the Extended Bayesian Skyline Plot with BEAST and with the cox1 data for both species. What I need is an alignment of the sequences.

So, first, extract the cox1 from the ddRAD sequences. And then, select them by population (in our case; LAKE)

```{bash LISTS, collapse = TRUE}
# AREG
BAM=../2023-05-18/BAM
EXCLUDE=../2023-05-23/VeryBad.txt

if [ ! -e AllArctic.list ]; then
   ls -1 $BAM/*.bam | grep -E "L|S" | grep -v -F -f $EXCLUDE > AllArctic.list
fi

## updated without hybrids or changed individuals
if [ ! -e FAR.list ]; then
  paste AllArctic.list ../2024-10-05/NGSadmix/ARCTIC.K2.qopt | \
  gawk '($2 > 0.999){print $1}' | grep -E "L" | xargs basename -s .bam > FAR.list
fi
if [ ! -e PSE.list ]; then
  paste AllArctic.list ../2024-10-05/NGSadmix/ARCTIC.K2.qopt | \
  gawk '($3 > 0.999){print $1}' | xargs basename -s .bam | grep -E 'S' > PSE.list
fi

if [ ! -e ARCTIC.list ]; then
  cat FAR.list PSE.list > ARCTIC_clean.list
fi

```

# Alignment and extraction of Cox for species

We had alreay several alignments to search the best extraction for
COI sequence in 2024-10-02.

I'm going to take those alignments and concatenate only the samples
that belong to one species.

```{bash}
FAR_ALIN=../2023-10-02/COI_Cpse_align.fa
PSE_ALIN=../2023-10-02/COI_Cpse_align.fa

if [ ! -e AlignCOI_FAR_00.fa ]; then
  grep -A 1 -Ff FAR.list $FAR_ALIN > AlignCOI_FAR_00.fa
fi

if [ ! -e AlignCOI_PSE_00.fa ]; then
  grep -A 1 -Ff PSE.list $PSE_ALIN > AlignCOI_PSE_00.fa
fi

```

And then, align them:

```{bash CREPI_ALIGN, results='hide'}
FOLDER=Alignments
if [ ! -d $FOLDER ]; then mkdir $FOLDER; fi
for i in FAR PSE; do
  if [ ! -e $FOLDER/AlignCOI_${i}_01.fa ]; then
    mafft --maxiterate 1000 --thread 24 --localpair AlignCOI_${i}_00.fa > $FOLDER/AlignCOI_${i}_01.fa
  fi
done
```

```{r}
if (file.exists("Alignments/AlignCOI_FAR.fa") == FALSE) {
  Align <- readDNAStringSet("Alignments/AlignCOI_FAR_01.fa")
  BrowseSeqs(Align)
  BrowseSeqs(subseq(Align, start = 219, end = 532))
  Align <- subseq(Align, start = 219, end = 532)
  writeXStringSet(Align, "Alignments/AlignCOI_FAR.fa")
}
```

```{bash}
FOLDER=Alignments
#if [ ! -e $FOLDER/AlignCOI_FAR.fa ]; then
#  Gblocks $FOLDER/AlignCOI_FAR_01.fa -t=d -b1=18 -b2=18 -e=-gb -d=y -v=1085 -b5=h
#  mv $FOLDER/AlignCOI_FAR_01.fa-gb $FOLDER/AlignCOI_FAR.fa
#fi

if [ ! -e $FOLDER/AlignCOI_PSE.fa ]; then
  Gblocks $FOLDER/AlignCOI_PSE_01.fa -t=d -e=-gb -v=1000
  mv $FOLDER/AlignCOI_PSE_01.fa-gb $FOLDER/AlignCOI_PSE.fa
fi
```


## Choosing the nucleotide susbstituion models
In principle, the *cox1* gene should be evolving in similar ways across lakes.
However, the amount of information available is different among lakes, so that
a simpler model may be better for lakes with fewer sequences. Below, I run
`modelTest()` (from `phangorn`) in every alignment and determine the best model
in each case.

```{r modelTest, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library('phangorn')
bestModels <- list()
for (pop in c('FAR', 'PSE')) {
   cox1 <- phyDat(as.DNAbin(suppressWarnings(readDNAStringSet(paste0('Alignments/AlignCOI_', pop, '.fa')))))
   Models <- modelTest(cox1, model = c('JC', 'HKY', 'TrN', 'GTR'),
                       control = pml.control(epsilon = 1e-08, maxit = 10, trace = 0, tau = 1e-08))
   bestModels[[pop]] <- as.pml(Models)
}
bestModels
```

## Running BEAST

First, you need to make the input file for Beast with Beauti, with all the
specifications like model, number of generations, and other population parameters.

```{bash eval = FALSE}

## Running the fist chain 

for i in LAN SUO; do
  if [ ! -e ${i}/EBSP.log ]; then
    beast -prefix ${i}/ -threads 4 -resume ${i}/$i.xml &> ${i}/screenlog.txt &
  fi
done
wait

## Running the second chain

for i in LAN SUO; do
  if [ ! -e ${i}/chain2.log ]; then
    beast -prefix ${i}/ -threads 4 ${i}/chain2.xml &> ${i}/screenlog2.txt &
  fi
done
wait

```

### Plot the EBSP
## First attempt
First chain
```{r FCHAIN}
source("/nata/mar/phyllodistomum/bin/plotEBSP.R") ## Modify the script to change the color in the plot

POP <- c("LAN", "SUO", "ARCTIC")
COL <- c("yellow2", "royalblue", "darkblue")
for (i in 1:length(POP)) {
  plotEBSP(paste0("EBSP01/", POP[i], "/EBSP.log"),
           useHPD = FALSE,
           log = "y",
           burnin = 0.1,
           plotPopFunctions = FALSE,
           popFunctionAlpha = 0.05,
           col = COL[i],
           #main = paste0(POP[i]), 
           xlab = "Time (M years)",
           ylab = "Ne",
           showLegend = FALSE)
}

```
